title: gdpr.erasure.open
description: Open an erasure for one subject, from a service that is NOT this one. The owner that detects the need (a retention purge in stapel-recordings, a host's delete view in another service) cannot reach GDPROrchestrator.request_erasure in-process, and this is the fire-and-forget half of the answer: it opens the same request, with the same per-owner receipt slots and the same purge SLA, that POST /erasures opens. Nothing comes back — a caller that needs the request id synchronously calls the gdpr.erasure.request Function instead. Authorization is NOT re-checked here: reaching the bus is the credential, exactly as for every other Action, so the emitting service owns the ownership question the way the ERASURE_AUTHORIZER seam owns it on the HTTP path. Delivery is at-least-once, so send idempotency_key: a repeat of the same key returns the request that already exists rather than minting a second erasure for one subject.

subject_type.description: One of STAPEL_GDPR["SUBJECT_TYPES"]. Anything else is refused — a typo'd subject would produce a request no owner can ever answer, which looks exactly like an owner that went silent.

subject_key.description: The host's own id for that subject (a user id for "account").

workspace_id.description: Workspace the subject belongs to, for owners that partition their stores by it.

requested_by.description: User id of whoever asked, when a person did. Empty for platform-initiated erasures.

origin.description: Why this erasure exists. Defaults to "user".

idempotency_key.description: De-duplication key, unique across erasures. Same key = same request. Empty opts out, which under at-least-once delivery means a redelivery opens a second erasure for the same subject.
